decks.title: Everyday Spelling Warm-Up
decks.instructions: Listen carefully, type each word, and build confidence with everyday school and home vocabulary.

words.definition: A place where children go to learn.
words.exampleSentence: The children arrived at school early in the morning.
words.hint: It begins with s and ends with l.

words.definition: A piece of ground where flowers or plants grow.
words.exampleSentence: We planted tomatoes in the garden behind the house.
words.hint: It has two syllables and starts with g.

words.definition: An opening in a wall fitted with glass.
words.exampleSentence: Please open the window and let fresh air inside.
words.hint: It begins with w and has the word win at the start.

words.definition: A large cloth used for warmth on a bed.
words.exampleSentence: She covered the baby with a soft blanket.
words.hint: It starts with bl and ends with et.

words.definition: The early part of the day before noon.
words.exampleSentence: We read our storybook every morning.
words.hint: It begins with m and has ing at the end.

words.definition: Very pleasing to look at or hear.
words.exampleSentence: The garden looked beautiful after the rain.
words.hint: It starts with beau and has three syllables.

words.definition: Kind and pleasant to others.
words.exampleSentence: Our new neighbour is friendly and cheerful.
words.hint: It ends with ly and starts with fr.

words.definition: Having great value or meaning.
words.exampleSentence: It is important to listen when the teacher speaks.
words.hint: It begins with im and ends with ant.

decks.instructions: Practise science-related words that help you talk about the world around you.

words.definition: The invisible mixture of gases around us.
words.exampleSentence: Plants, animals, and people all need air to live.
words.hint: It is a short word with three letters.

words.definition: A living thing that grows in soil or water.
words.exampleSentence: We watered the plant after class.
words.hint: It starts with pl.

words.definition: A living thing that can move and breathe.
words.exampleSentence: A goat is an animal that lives on many farms.
words.hint: It begins with a and has three syllables.

words.definition: The condition of the air at a certain time.
words.exampleSentence: The weather is sunny today.
words.hint: It begins with wea.

words.definition: To carry people or goods from one place to another.
words.exampleSentence: Buses transport children safely to school.
words.hint: It begins with trans.

words.definition: The natural world and surroundings where we live.
words.exampleSentence: We should keep the environment clean.
words.hint: It starts with en and ends with ment.

decks.instructions: Strengthen your classroom language with words you meet in reading, science, and social studies.

words.definition: A number that shows part of a whole.
words.exampleSentence: One half is a fraction.
words.hint: It starts with fr and ends with tion.

words.definition: A group of related sentences on one main idea.
words.exampleSentence: Write one paragraph about your favourite season.
words.hint: It begins with para.

words.definition: A scientific test done to learn something.
words.exampleSentence: The class did an experiment with water and ice.
words.hint: It starts with ex and ends with ment.

words.definition: Travel from one place to another.
words.exampleSentence: The family began a long journey by train.
words.hint: It contains our.

decks.title: Advanced Word Power
decks.instructions: Practise mature academic words that appear across subjects and formal writing.

words.definition: Detailed examination of something.
words.exampleSentence: Her analysis of the poem was thoughtful and clear.
words.hint: It starts with ana.

words.definition: An idea that can be tested.
words.exampleSentence: The student wrote a hypothesis before the experiment.
words.hint: It begins with hypo.

words.definition: A duty or task that one is expected to do.
words.exampleSentence: Leadership comes with responsibility.
words.hint: It ends with ility.

cards.back: Air is the invisible mixture of gases all around us. People, animals, and plants need it to live.
We cannot usually see air, but we can feel it when the wind blows or a fan is on.
Air is important because living things need it for breathing and burning.

cards.front: Name one place where air is found.
cards.back: Air is found everywhere around us, including in the classroom, at home, and outdoors.

cards.front: How can moving air help us?
cards.back: Moving air can cool us, dry clothes, and help seeds spread.

cards.front: Give one example of air in action.
cards.back: A balloon fills up because air goes inside it.
A plant is a living thing that grows in soil or water and makes its own food.

cards.front: What do plants need to grow?
cards.back: Plants need air, sunlight, water, and soil or nutrients to grow well.

cards.front: Name one part of a plant.
cards.back: Some parts of a plant are the root, stem, leaf, flower, and fruit.
The root holds the plant in the soil and takes in water and nutrients.
Plants give us food, shade, medicine, and clean air.

cards.front: Give one example of a plant product.
cards.back: Fruit, vegetables, wood, and cotton all come from plants.
Transportation is the movement of people and goods from one place to another.

cards.front: Name the three main types of transportation.
cards.back: The three main types are land transportation, water transportation, and air transportation.

cards.front: Give one example of land transportation.
cards.back: Examples include bus, car, bicycle, train, and motorcycle.

cards.front: Give one example of water transportation.
cards.back: Examples include canoe, boat, ferry, and ship.
Transportation helps people travel to school, work, hospitals, shops, and other communities.

cards.front: What safety rule should we follow when using transport?
cards.back: We should obey road and transport safety rules, board carefully, and respect drivers and other passengers.
A noun is a naming word for a person, place, animal, or thing.
A pronoun is a word used in place of a noun, such as he, she, it, or they.
A verb is an action word or a being word. It tells what someone does or is.
An adjective is a describing word. It tells us more about a noun.
An adverb tells how, when, where, or how often something happens.

cards.front: Why are parts of speech important?
cards.back: They help us understand the job each word is doing so we can read, write, and speak clearly.
Multiplication means adding equal groups again and again.
6 x 1 = 6 because any number multiplied by 1 stays the same.
4 x 0 = 0 because any number multiplied by 0 equals 0.
Multiplication helps us count quickly and solve repeated addition problems.
Evaporation happens when liquid water changes into water vapour because of heat.
Condensation happens when water vapour cools and turns back into tiny droplets.
Precipitation is water falling from clouds as rain, snow, hail, or sleet.

cards.front: Why is the water cycle important?
cards.back: It moves water around Earth and helps supply water for plants, animals, and people.
Collection happens when water gathers in rivers, lakes, oceans, and the ground.

cards.front: What gives energy for the water cycle?
cards.back: The Sun provides the heat energy that starts much of the water cycle.
A simile compares two things using like or as.
A metaphor compares two things by saying one thing is another.
Personification gives human qualities to animals, objects, or ideas.

cards.front: Why do writers use figures of speech?
cards.back: They make writing more vivid, imaginative, and memorable.

cards.front: Give an example of a simile.
cards.back: "As brave as a lion" is a simile.

cards.front: How is a metaphor different from a simile?
cards.back: A simile uses like or as, but a metaphor does not.
Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight to make food from carbon dioxide and water.
It takes place mainly in the chloroplasts of green plant cells.
Chlorophyll traps light energy needed for photosynthesis.

cards.front: What are the raw materials of photosynthesis?
cards.back: The raw materials are water and carbon dioxide.

cards.front: What are the products of photosynthesis?
cards.back: The products are glucose and oxygen.

cards.front: Why is photosynthesis important to life?
cards.back: It provides food for plants and releases oxygen needed by most living things.
